conventions.convention: CSS codes use C₂ ⊆ C₁, with coset states indexed by C₁/C₂, X checks from C₂, and Z checks from C₁⊥. No additional C₂⊥ ⊆ C₁ hypothesis is imposed.
Stabilizers are abelian groups of Hermitian phase-aware Paulis, exclude −I, and define the common +1 eigenspace.

Encoder coordinates and circuit wires are zero-based; supplier Pauli factor j corresponds to circuit wire j−1. Gates are appended chronologically, and every tableau update retains the exact phase modulo four.
A syndrome bit is the exponent in Egⱼ = (−1)^sⱼ gⱼE. Logical Pauli classes quotient the Pauli centralizer by scalar phases times stabilizers.
Distance minimizes Pauli weight over N(S) outside ZₙS; for a code encoding zero qubits, distance is +∞.

The surface patch has d ≥ 2, removes the left and right vertical boundary edges and their vertices from the relative chain coordinates, retains 2d² physical edges, and uses vertex X checks and face Z checks.
The CSS correction theorem uses δ({0}) = +∞ locally while retaining the classical convention d({0}) = n+1.

load_bearing.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and let S be an abelian group of Hermitian n-qubit Pauli operators with −I ∉ S, generated by r independent checks. The average P_S = |S|⁻¹Σg∈S g is the orthogonal projector onto the stabilizer code space and has rank 2^(n−r).

For C₂ ⊆ C₁ ≤ F₂ⁿ, n ≥ 1, the coset vectors encode k = dim C₁−dim C₂ logical qubits isometrically and equal the common +1 eigenspace of X checks from C₂ and Z checks from C₁⊥. The theorem also gives the exact dual-coset Hadamard transform with coefficient 2^(−k/2).

For an n-qubit stabilizer group generated by r independent commuting Hermitian checks with −I excluded, N(S)/(ZₙS) is a binary vector space of dimension 2(n−r), nontrivial exactly when the code encodes at least one qubit.

Every Pauli of weight less than d(S) is scalar on the code when it belongs to ZₙS, or is detected by a stabilizer check. A finite channel with Kraus operators in the span of weight-at-most-t Paulis is correctable whenever 2t < d(S).

The phase-aware pivot procedure returns a chronological Clifford gate list D, its reversed adjoint encoder list, and signed row-operation data (M, κ), with exact input-combination rows Gᵢ satisfying DGᵢD† = +Zᵢ.

The relative d×d patch encodes one logical qubit and has distance d. Nontrivial Z logical supports contain a rough-to-rough path of length at least d; nontrivial X logical supports contain a top-to-bottom dual path of length at least d+1. The stated self-avoiding path count is at most (d+1)3^ℓ.
For every binary linear code C ≤ F₂ⁿ with n ≥ 1, dim C⊥ = n−dim C. This argument uses no form of the Axiom of Choice.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite-dimensional dimension, including dimension zero and the dependence on the scalar field.
Choice-free finite basis extension, subspace dimension bounds, and equality of a subspace with its ambient space when finite dimensions agree.
Coordinate dual bases and equality of finite-dimensional vector-space and algebraic-dual dimensions.
Binary dual dimensions, symplectic annihilator dimensions, and ranks and kernels of the relative patch matrices.
Identifying the self-adjoint stabilizer average as the orthogonal projector onto its image.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 says that the Knill–Laflamme theorem yields recovery for a finite Pauli error family, whereas the cited theorem assumes Kraus operators of a trace-preserving channel. The unscaled Pauli family generally is not such a Kraus family. Normalizing a nonempty family of m Paulis by 1/√m supplies the missing channel; the final application in 3.1 already concerns the actual channel from the Statement. This is a short missing justification, not a counterexample to the claim.

seams_checked.note: Encoder lists use singleton chronological layers with the last-applied matrix on the left. Syndrome extraction uses observed projective outcomes and assigns conditional states only on positive-probability branches.

Column-vector generator and parity-check shapes, bilinear duals, and classical uniqueness radii are preserved. The CSS theorem explicitly distinguishes its infinite zero-code correction radius from the supplier's finite distance sentinel.
CNOT control-target order and SWAP as an actual state permutation agree with the suppliers. The encoder explicitly translates zero-based circuit wires to one-based Pauli factors.

The channel-level conclusions use finite Kraus scalar compression and nonzero code spaces, matching the recovery theorem. The intermediate unnormalized-family invocation is recorded separately as a short proof gap.
The X-before-Z phase convention, exact product rule, Hermitian parity criterion, symplectic commutator, and H/S/CNOT conjugation updates match the opened supplier statements.
The displayed Y sign and exact H, S and X matrices are preserved. S† is explicitly admitted in the encoder alphabet.
Computational basis ordering, ordered tensor factors, the linear-first inner product, and the one-dimensional empty register are respected, including zero logical qubits.
The subgroup label injection, finite group-average projector, and projector-rank theorem apply to exactly the Hermitian abelian groups excluding −I used here.

The concatenated Steane lemma uses the exact CSS transform, projector dimension and 2t<distance recovery condition. Planar consumers use the same relative patch and crossing-path count under perfect syndrome extraction. The proper-code contract distinguishes correction capacity from stabilizer distance.
